questions.question:
Spot the part of the sentence that contains an error.

If there is no error, choose D.

A. She must have left

B. the office early yesterday

C. because she looks very tired today.

D. No error
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence shows a mismatch in tense and logical consistency between the clauses.
 
• The phrase "**must have left**" indicates a past deduction, referring to a completed action.
 
• However, "**looks very tired today**" refers to a present condition, which creates inconsistency when linked directly with a specific past time marker "**yesterday**".
 
• This inconsistency makes **part C** incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She must have left the office early because she **looked** very tired today."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "She must have left"** – This part is grammatically correct and properly expresses past deduction.
 
• **B: "the office early yesterday"** – This part is also correct and clearly indicates time.
 
• **D: "No error"** – This option is incorrect because there is an error in part C.

• **Option 2: "punk"** does not relate to a river or a place.

• **Option 4: "brink"** refers to the edge of something but is not commonly used to describe the side of a river.

**Complete Sentence:** *"The children played on the river **bank**__."*

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The novel which had remained unpublished for decades (1)/ was discovered by chance in a locked drawer (2)/ and were later translated into multiple languages (3)/ by a well-known critic. (4)

options.text: The novel which had remained unpublished for decades (1)
was discovered by chance in a locked drawer (2)
and were later translated into multiple languages (3)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is in **part (3)** of the sentence due to a **subject-verb agreement** violation.
 
• The subject of the sentence is "**The novel**," which is a singular noun.
 
• In a sentence with a compound predicate (two or more actions for the same subject), all verbs must agree with that subject. While the first verb "was discovered" (part 2) correctly matches the singular subject, the second verb "**were**" (part 3) is plural.
 
• The plural verb "were" must be replaced with the singular verb "**was**" to maintain grammatical consistency.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The novel which had remained unpublished for decades was discovered by chance in a locked drawer and **was** later translated into multiple languages by a well-known critic."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "The novel which had remained..."** – This part is correct. The past perfect tense ("had remained") correctly indicates an action that was completed before another past action (the discovery).
 
• **2: "was discovered by chance..."** – This is the correct singular passive voice construction matching the subject "The novel."
 
• **4: "by a well-known critic"** – This part is correct. The compound adjective "well-known" is properly hyphenated before the noun it modifies.
 
• **Grammar Tip:** When a sentence is long or contains intervening phrases (like "which had remained unpublished for decades"), always trace the verb back to the **main subject** to ensure they agree in number.

questions.question:
Change the following from active to passive:

We are preparing a detailed report on environmental hazards.

options.text: A detailed report on environmental hazards is being prepared by us.
We have prepared a detailed report on environmental hazards.
The report was prepared on environmental hazards by us.
A detailed report on environmental hazards has been prepared by us.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "We are preparing a detailed report on environmental hazards."
 
• This sentence is in the **Present Continuous** tense. The rule for conversion is: *Subject + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Object.*
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "A detailed report on environmental hazards" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "are preparing" to "is being prepared."
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "us."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"A detailed report on environmental hazards is being prepared by us."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"We have prepared a detailed report on environmental hazards." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to Present Perfect and remains in the active voice.
 
• **Option 3: **"The report was prepared on environmental hazards by us." – Incorrect because it uses the Past Simple tense.
 
• **Option 4: **"A detailed report on environmental hazards has been prepared by us." – Incorrect because it uses the Present Perfect Passive tense.

questions.question:
Change the following from active to passive:

They have adopted multiple strategies to enhance learning outcomes in rural schools.

options.text: Multiple strategies have been adopted to enhance learning outcomes in rural schools.
Multiple strategies are being adopted by them for better learning outcomes.
Multiple strategies were adopted by them.
Multiple strategies are adopted by them to improve learning.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "They have adopted multiple strategies to enhance learning outcomes in rural schools."
 
• This sentence is in the **Present Perfect** tense. The rule for conversion is: *Object + has/have + been + V3 (Past Participle) + (by + Subject).*
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "Multiple strategies" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "have adopted" to "have been adopted."
 
• The rest of the sentence ("to enhance learning outcomes in rural schools") follows the verb. Note that "by them" is optional and often omitted in passive voice when the agent is general or implied.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Multiple strategies have been adopted to enhance learning outcomes in rural schools."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"Multiple strategies are being adopted..." – Incorrect because "are being adopted" is the Present Continuous passive form.
 
• **Option 3: **"Multiple strategies were adopted..." – Incorrect because "were adopted" is the Past Simple passive form.
 
• **Option 4: **"Multiple strategies are adopted..." – Incorrect because "are adopted" is the Present Simple passive form.

questions.question:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The house had been painted by the workers before the rain started.

options.text: The workers had painted the house before the rain started.
The workers painted the house before the rain started.
The house was painted before the rain started.
The workers have painted the house before the rain started.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active voice structure: The agent (the doer of the action) becomes the subject of the sentence.
 
• In the passive voice, the sentence is: "The house had been painted by the workers before the rain started."
 
• The sentence is in the **Past Perfect** tense. The passive form is *had + been + V3*. To convert it to active voice, the structure is: *Subject + had + V3 + Object*.
 
• To convert to active voice: Place the agent "the workers" at the beginning as the subject.
 
• Change the passive verb "had been painted" to the active form "had painted."
 
• Place the original subject "the house" after the verb as the object.
 
• The subordinate clause "before the rain started" remains unchanged.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The workers had painted the house before the rain started."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"The workers painted the house..." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to Past Simple.
 
• **Option 3: **"The house was painted..." – Incorrect because it is still in the passive voice and changes the tense to Past Simple.
 
• **Option 4: **"The workers have painted the house..." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to Present Perfect.

questions.question:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The new policy will be implemented by the administration next month.

options.text: The administration will implement the new policy next month.
The administration is implementing the new policy.
The new policy was implemented by the administration.
The new policy has been implemented.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active voice structure: The agent (the doer of the action) becomes the subject of the sentence, followed by the base verb.
 
• In the passive voice, the sentence is: "The new policy will be implemented by the administration next month."
 
• The sentence is in the **Future Simple** tense. The passive form is *will + be + V3 (Past Participle)*. To convert it to active voice, the structure is: *Subject + will + V1 (Base Form) + Object*.
 
• To convert to active voice: Identify the agent "the administration" and place it at the beginning as the subject.
 
• Change the passive verb "will be implemented" to the active form "will implement."
 
• Place the original subject "the new policy" after the verb as the object.
 
• The time phrase "next month" remains at the end for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The administration will implement the new policy next month."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"The administration is implementing..." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to Present Continuous.
 
• **Option 3: **"The new policy was implemented..." – Incorrect because it remains in the passive voice and changes the tense to Past Simple.
 
• **Option 4: **"The new policy has been implemented." – Incorrect because it remains in the passive voice and changes the tense to Present Perfect.

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

She said, "I will help you with your homework."

options.text: She said that she will help me.
She said that she would help me with my homework.
She said she will be helping with homework.
She said she would helping my homework.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She said that she would help me with my homework.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"I will help" becomes "she would help"**
 
 
• The pronoun **"I"** (subject) changes to **"she"** to refer back to the original speaker.
 
• The modal **"will"** changes to its past form **"would"** because the reporting verb ("said") is in the past tense.
 
 
 
• **"you" and "your" become "me" and "my"**
 
 
• The object **"you"** and possessive adjective **"your"** change to **"me"** and **"my"** to reflect the listener's perspective in reported speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• The reporting verb **"said"** remains the same, often followed by the conjunction **"that"** to introduce the reported clause.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She said that she would help me with my homework."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "She said that she will help me." 

 
 
• **Error:** Fails to change the tense of the modal verb; "will" must change to "would" when the reporting verb is in the past.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "She said she will be helping with homework." 
 
 
• **Error:** Incorrectly changes the aspect to continuous ("will be helping") and fails to apply the backshift to the past tense.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She said she would helping my homework." 
 
 
• **Error:** Grammatically incorrect; the modal "would" must be followed by the base form of the verb ("help"), not the present participle ("helping").

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

He said that he was feeling unwell.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** He said, "I am feeling unwell."
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"was feeling" becomes "am feeling"**
 
 
• In the transition from indirect to direct speech, we reverse the "backshift." Since the indirect speech uses the **Past Continuous** ("was feeling"), the direct speech must use the **Present Continuous** ("am feeling").
 
 
 
• **Pronoun "he" becomes "I"**
 
 
• The pronoun **"he"** in the reported clause refers to the speaker, so it changes back to the first-person pronoun **"I"** in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation:**
 
 
• Direct speech requires the use of a comma after the reporting verb and the placement of the spoken words within quotation marks, starting with a capital letter.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said, “I am feeling unwell.”"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "He said, 'I will feel unwell.'" 

 
 
• **Error:** Uses the future tense, which would have been reported as "would be feeling" or "would feel."
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He said, 'I have felt unwell.'" 
 
 
• **Error:** Uses the Present Perfect tense, which would change to the Past Perfect ("had felt") in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He said, 'I felt unwell.'" 
 
 
• **Error:** Uses the Past Simple tense. In indirect speech, this typically shifts to the Past Perfect ("had felt").

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate adverb.

Mohan is ________ shy. He cannot communicate with people freely.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**truly**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The adverb "**truly**" emphasizes the depth or extent of a characteristic (in this case, "shy").
 
• The sentence implies that Mohan is extremely shy and struggles to communicate freely, making "**truly**" the most appropriate choice.
 
• **Option 2: "moderately"** suggests a mild degree, which does not align with the context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3: "rather"** suggests hesitation or slight emphasis, which is weaker than the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 4: "naturally"** is incorrect because the sentence focuses on the degree of shyness, not its origin.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"Mohan is **truly**__ shy. He cannot communicate with people freely."*

questions.question: Choose the correct one word substitution for: "A belief that the universe and all existence are divine"
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Pantheism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Pantheism"** refers to the belief that the universe and all existence are divine, meaning that God or divinity is present in everything around us. (सर्वेश्वरवाद)
 
 
 
• **Example:** The philosophy of pantheism emphasizes the interconnectedness of all living beings and the universe as a manifestation of divine power.
 
 
 
• **"Pantheism"** often equates the concept of God with the universe itself, suggesting that everything is a part of the divine essence. (सर्वेश्वरवाद)
 
 
 
• **Example:** Many ancient cultures practiced pantheism by worshipping nature as divine.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Pantheism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Polytheism** (बहुदेववाद): The belief in or worship of multiple gods.
 
 
 
• **Example:** Ancient Greeks practiced polytheism, worshipping gods like Zeus, Athena, and Apollo.
 
 

 
• **Mysticism** (रहस्यवाद): The belief or practice involving seeking direct communion with divine or spiritual truths, often through meditation or contemplation.
 
 
 
• **Example:** Mysticism is common in many religious traditions, where individuals seek personal experiences of the divine.
 
 

 
• **Agnosticism** (अज्ञेयवाद): The belief that the existence of God or the divine is unknown or unknowable.
 
 
 
• **Example:** He adopted agnosticism because he felt that the existence of God could neither be proven nor disproven.
